The purpose of this phase of the program is to stimulate the landowners to:
a. identify their drainage requirements
recognize their responsibility, as well as that of the Division
c. develop a willingness to reach a mutual solution 
   develop a line of communication between the Division and landowners, and vice versa.
PECHNICAL ASSISTANCE
After many of the drainage problems have been identified in the educational phase of the program, it is necessary for the individual landowners to determine their agricultural drainage requirements and to develop drainage plans. The Soil Conservation Service will provide engineering and agronomic assistance to accomplish this objective. If needed, the Cooperative Extension Service may provide additional assistance.
After the formal drainage plans have been formulated, they should be submitted to the District Highway Office for consideration. If such formal drainage plans are approved, the common facilities will be incorporated into the final nighway plan.
DEVELOPMENT OF DRAINAGE PLAN
Upon receipt of the proposed drainage requirements, the Highway District Engineer should consider such needs in the development of the preliminary highway plan. Upon completion of the preliminary plan, a meeting should be called for review. If agreement is reached, the proposal would be incorporated in the final plans. If agreement cannot be reached, those items in question would revert back to the local people for further study and referral to the Highway District Engineer.
IMPLEMENTATION OF FINAL PLANS
The Division has the primary responsibility for implementing all drainage activities within the limits of the highway right of way. The soil and water conservation district, with assistance from the Soil Conservation Service, has the primary responsibility for providing technical assistance
